package_info.why_malicious: The package is vulnerable to uncontrolled resource consumption (CVE-2021-22119). It allows an attacker to create an unlimited number of abandoned OAuth2 authorization requests, which are stored indefinitely in the session without expiration or limit, leading to potential denial of service (DoS) by exhausting system resources.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Stores each new OAuth2 authorization request in the session, keyed by state, without any limit or expiration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code allows an unbounded number of authorization requests to be stored in the session, with no checks on the number or expiration of requests.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would be to limit the number of stored requests per session or enforce expiration to prevent resource exhaustion. The actual behavior allows unlimited accumulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Storing a single or a small, bounded number of authorization requests per session is legitimate for tracking OAuth2 flows.
key_indicators: No limit on the number of stored requests
No expiration or cleanup of abandoned requests
Direct mapping of user input (state) to session storage

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends repeated OAuth2 authorization requests to the application, each with a unique state.
attack_chain.leads_to: Each request is stored in the session, accumulating indefinitely.

attack_chain.action: Attacker aborts the authorization flow before completion, leaving requests abandoned in the session.
attack_chain.leads_to: Abandoned requests are never cleaned up or expired.

attack_chain.action: System resources (memory, session storage) are exhausted as the number of stored requests grows.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of Service (DoS) condition for legitimate users.

behavioral_signatures: Unbounded growth of session attributes related to OAuth2 authorization requests
Repeated creation of session entries keyed by unique state values
Absence of expiration or cleanup logic for stored authorization requests
file_indicators: Session attributes named after OAuth2 authorization requests
network_indicators: High volume of OAuth2 authorization requests from a single user or IP
Repeated incomplete or aborted OAuth2 flows
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor session storage for unbounded growth in the number of OAuth2 authorization requests per session. Look for session attributes that accumulate without cleanup. Detect high-frequency, incomplete OAuth2 authorization attempts from the same user or IP. Review application code for use of vulnerable versions of spring-security-oauth2-client and absence of request limiting or expiration logic.
